thread:
eva (sec-eng): quick heads-up — ran canary restore of prod DB snapshots after last CMK rotation and hit decrypt errors on 1/3 restores. AccessDenied during kms:Decrypt.

sree (dbops): any logs or request ids?

eva (sec-eng): excerpt from the restore job: 
```
ERROR: restore failed: AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/restore-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
RequestId: 8a1f2c3d-xyz
```

simon (infra): was snapshot created before or after the rotation job? what was the grant TTL?

eva (sec-eng): snapshot timestamp 2026-03-20T23:30Z (pre-rotate). CMK rotation completed 2026-03-21T00:05Z. grant TTL on uploader appears to be 30m so it expired ~00:31Z. restore attempted ~01:10Z.

nancy (compliance): our encryptops runbook says ephemeral grants should survive a reasonable restore window. Do we have a documented minimum TTL?

devops-bot: alert: backup-uploader-prod grant issued at 2026-03-21T00:01Z, expires 2026-03-21T00:31Z.

sree (dbops): quick recovery path: recreate a grant for the backup-uploader role against the CMK used to encrypt that snapshot, then restart the restore job. Longer term we should either extend grant TTL or grant via CMK key policy/iam role so restores don't rely on one-off grants.

eva (sec-eng): I tried to find CloudTrail PutGrant events around rotate but there are gaps. CloudTrail shows PutGrant at 00:01 and then nothing near the time of rotate; ingestion lag suspected. We need reliable audit records for grant lifecycle.

simon (infra): action item: check snapshot metadata object in s3 (redwood-backups/prod/.../encryption_metadata.json). It stores grant_id and key_id. If grant_id present we can call RevokeGrant/RetireGrant carefully, or create new grant using key_id + grantee. Be careful not to orphan snapshots.

sree (dbops): commands I used to repro/create grant locally: 
```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader-prod \
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt \
  --name "backup-upload-grant"
```
then re-run restore job.

eva (sec-eng): proposed runbook updates:
- short: re-grant backup-uploader-prod for affected snapshots and rerun canaries immediately.
- medium: update backup-uploader to request longer-lived grants (e.g., 7d) or add an IAM allow on the CMK for the backup principal so restores are not tied to ephemeral grants.
- medium: add CloudTrail-based alerting for PutGrant failures or unexpected grant-retire events.
- long: augment snapshot metadata with rotation-safe fallback token (e.g., alternate key-id or a grant-refresh helper) and CI test for upload->rotation->restore.

nancy (compliance): please create a compliance ticket listing affected tenants and dates; we need to assess exposure and update audit trail.

sree (dbops): re-grant completed for the affected snapshots, retried canary restores: 2/2 succeeded. I will open a PR to bump grant TTL and add CI test.

eva (sec-eng): awesome. add a unit test in the uploader repo that simulates a CMK rotation window and validates restore still succeeds. Tag @simon for infra guardrails. :thumbsup:

simon (infra): will add an infra check that blocks CMK rotation if there are snapshots with grants < 24h TTL and will add CloudWatch metric for PutGrant churn.

devops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0453 (snapshot-grant-expiry). assignees: sree, eva, simon, nancy.

eva (sec-eng): I'll draft the runbook updates and push to encryptops playbook.

nancy (compliance): putting this into JIRA: COMP-712 for review.

sree (dbops): left a note in snapshot metadata: "grant_refresh_needed: true" for affected objects.

eva (sec-eng): thanks everyone. follow-ups: PRs from sree + simon, compliance ticket from nancy, and runbook PR from me.

(end of thread)
